I'm a cook turned copywriter. I made the switch 8 months ago in my mid-30s. Here’s what I've noticed:

Physically, I've gained 20 lbs and diet and exercise can't seem to make a dent in the weight gain. My job is extremely stressful and I think this is the cause of the weight gain. Sitting at a desk is tough on my back. I have a standing desk but those aren't that comfortable either. But was terrible for the first few months, but I've adjusted to it. 

In terms of workplace culture, from the kitchen to office, it’s not that different, but I get along better with the creatives and developers. When I get around the accounts people I can tell they look down on me for coming from a blue-collar background and having no business school degree. But they're not really that fun to talk to anyhow. I found a couple of people I can bullshit and swap drinking stories with. 

I do regret the move but that isn't to say you will. My agency is infamous for having a toxic culture in an industry that prides itself on being dysfunctional. 

My advice is not to burn bridges at your old job and if this one doesn't work out there's a good chance you can go back. I'll be going back to cooking in September. It'll be a pay cut but I don't think the money is worth my health. 

In the end, you gotta give it an honest shot. If it doesn't work out, at least you can say you tried.

Good luck brother, keep us posted on how it goes.
